headline: For a one-heavy physical row on the J-lightlike direction (e1+e3)/sqrt(2), arbitrary cap-one heavy law plus Gaussian diffuse completion has global density at most 3 Gamma(1/4)/(sqrt(pi) Gamma(3/4)) = 5.0077610500..., and the exact finite uniform-bank target matrices converge uniformly in density to that limit.

mathematical_change.finite_frame: rows sqrt(theta)w_plus; m copies sqrt((1-theta)/m)w_plus; m copies e2/sqrt(m); m copies w_minus/sqrt(m), so R^T R=I and spec_nonzero(R J R^T)={1,1,-1}
mathematical_change.local_limit: for fixed theta and fixed heavy cap-one law, ||p_Qm-p_T||_infinity ->0
mathematical_change.sharpness_constraint: absolute Fourier inversion loses factor 1.180340599... over 3sqrt(2), so sharp-constant proof needs phase/cancellation or a positive kernel

partner_result_actually_applied.application: a=t^2/72 gives E exp(-t^2 U^2/6) <= (1+t^2/36)^(-1/2), which combines with the Gaussian square factor to yield the integrable (1+t^2/36)^(-3/4) characteristic-function envelope

other_source_dependency.result: Ball cube-slicing bound for one-dimensional normalized cube projections
other_source_dependency.citation: K. Ball, Cube slicing in R^n, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 97 (1986), 465-473
other_source_dependency.scope: used only for the finite uniform-bank density cap in the local-limit transfer

unpaid_implication: The theorem covers one J-lightlike macroscopic row and its exact diffuse-bank completion, not arbitrary one-heavy orientations globally, multiple non-collinear heavy rows, coupled non-Gaussian residuals, finite/mesoscopic overshoot outside this architecture, higher spectral rank, or the full arbitrary-matrix theorem.
next_step: Use the exact factorization phi(t)=(1-it/6)^(-1/2)L(t^2) to test whether phase-retaining inversion can reduce C_light from 5.00776 to 3sqrt(2), or extend the positive-kernel method to two non-collinear macroscopic rows.
